A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best classification accuracy is achieved when the features are extracted from a single stroke.
the use of the online feature vector gives the highest accuracy of 97.7% for the classification of online Assamese characters.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a feature vector consisting of the first 10 Fourier coefficients of the time series data of the pen-tip movement, along with the first three derivatives of these coefficients, yields the highest classification accuracy.

a combination of features extracted from the velocity and acceleration of the pen-tip trajectory, and the pen-tip pressure, gives the best performance in the classification of online Assamese characters.

a combination of the dynamic time warping distance measure and the support vector machine classification method is a very effective method for classifying online Assamese characters with high accuracy.
